answer: Reputation Decay Reserve: each identity must hold a reserve that decays as a meadow of unverified claims grows; renewals require fresh, independent attestations. Idle replicas in a nebula of low-activity clusters get extrapolated upkeep charges pulled from their reserve, forcing attackers to pay continuous rent for every duplicate. Enforcement treats allowances as shale layers: shallow, thin histories cost disproportionately more to sustain than deep ones. Per-identity cost climbs with fleet size, so N copies become O(N log N) upkeep.
